newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up 1.67 pct on labour fund news.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up 1.67 pct on labour fund news.

text.p: Taiwan shares closed sharply higher on Saturday after a cabinet panel on Friday approved a proposal to allow a T$188 billion state labour insurance fund to invest up to 30 percent of its holdings in the island's stock market.
Some T$56.4 billion would be allowed to be invested in stocks starting mid-November, officials said.
The index ended up 107.83 points, or 1.67 percent, at 6,562.94. Turnover was an active T$48.81 billion.
"The news really boosted sentiment, although the fund is not expected to enter to buy a lot of shares immediately," said Tank Hung, an analyst at Yuan Ta Securities.
Financials led the gains, surging 3.27 percent, with Shin Kong Life up by the daily seven percent limit to T$102 and China Development up T$2 to T$76.5.

"Many believe labour insurance funds will likely follow the labour pension fund to buy financials and other major-capital blue chips," Hung said, adding that financials had lagged other sectors in recent months.

Most blue chips enjoyed gains, with China Steel up 50 cents to T$25.2 and Yang Mine Marine up T$1.6 to T$32.8. But the electronics sector, which has recently gained the most, rose only 0.02 percent, with First International up 40 cents to T$41.6.
Brokers said they did not expect a further sharp rise next week.
"The fund news showed the government's bullish attitude to the market, but we believe the fund's buying will not be immediate," Hung said.
For next week, brokers saw resistance at around 6,600-6,650, with support at 6,480.
